summary: SL-020 built the whole foundation of filesystem-analyser-v2 from an empty tree. That was the SDK 10 bootstrap (eng/dotnet.ps1), the Win32 directory reader, the tag-based link classifier, the WOF/hardlink/large-file size probe, the struct-of-arrays ScanStore, a WPF window with drive buttons, a folder dialog and a CLI path argument, and 86 real-NTFS tests. Validate showed it works on real volumes: C:\ scanned in 83.6 s (3.45M files, 638 MiB peak), D:\ and SMB Z:\ finished, and the product agreed with an independent walk on C:\Windows and D:\. It took an unusually large number of laps to get there: critique, critique-review, build, code-review and validate each ran three times, design and spike twice. Most of that was a critique that ran after the build instead of before it, and two minor obligations that cost a whole extra build, review and validate lap.

payload.summary: SL-020 built the whole foundation of filesystem-analyser-v2 from an empty tree. That was the SDK 10 bootstrap (eng/dotnet.ps1), the Win32 directory reader, the tag-based link classifier, the WOF/hardlink/large-file size probe, the struct-of-arrays ScanStore, a WPF window with drive buttons, a folder dialog and a CLI path argument, and 86 real-NTFS tests. Validate showed it works on real volumes: C:\ scanned in 83.6 s (3.45M files, 638 MiB peak), D:\ and SMB Z:\ finished, and the product agreed with an independent walk on C:\Windows and D:\. It took an unusually large number of laps to get there: critique, critique-review, build, code-review and validate each ran three times, design and spike twice. Most of that was a critique that ran after the build instead of before it, and two minor obligations that cost a whole extra build, review and validate lap.
payload.estimate_error: Both the size and the tier were wrong, in different ways. Size (medium) was too small: it covered scaffold and SDK bootstrap, native interop, store, scanner, WPF window and 86 tests from an empty tree, and every gate needed 2 to 3 runs. It should have been cut into scaffold/scanner-core/window, or sized large. Tier: the slice opened as low, and Q-002 raised it to medium because the project constraint says scanner slices get harder review. The header then reads "medium · high risk", but critique #1 and critique-review #1 were still skipped as "low-risk slice in a minimal project". The tier that gated the process was the stale one. The critique first ran after build #1 and reviewed a design that already existed as running code.
what_went_wrong: Critique #1 and critique-review #1 were skipped as low-risk after Q-002 had raised the tier. The first real adversarial review came after build #1, so its 3 majors and 11 minors turned into build #2 (12 obligations) on built code. Reviewing the design would have cost less than reworking the build.

The critique ran on a built tree but reviewed the design text. 2 of its 14 findings (m2 empty FAT root, m3 offline fixture) were already fixed in the code, and m11 was pure doc drift. M2's claim that SizeProbe builds the charged record's path was wrong: Scanner.cs:159 builds the repeat name's own path. The critique-review then re-graded two of the three majors (M1, M2) to minor. M3's flushed-writer case was measured as fine by the documentary test.

Build #2's own fixes produced the next round's findings. The O-004 fix added a third probe case (listed at 64 MiB or more) with a cloud guard no test pinned (code-review m1). The O-008 fix caught ArgumentException wide enough to swallow ScanStore's ArgumentOutOfRangeException (code-review m2). Both cost a third lap.

Code-review #2 passed with O-014 and O-015 still accepted-pending. Validate #1 then ran the full real-drive battery (C:\ scan, D:\, publish, cross-checks) and halted on 'the two fixes are not in the tree'. Validate #2 failed on the same fact. Validate #3 finally passed. Two minor obligations cost build #3, code-review #3 and validate #3.

The engine's guard began refusing UI Automation partway through the slice. Attempts 1 and 2 had used UIA to read the window's endings. Build #3 could not smoke-test the O-015 filter, and validate substituted a throwaway in-process WPF harness in %TEMP%. The published exe's own window was never read, and the App has no test project or machine-readable outcome.

The design text drifted from the build in at least five places: HashSet vs custom open-addressing FileId index, ServerGarbageCollector vs ServerGarbageCollection, a deny-ReadAttributes ACE fixture that does not block a FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES open, an unflushed sparse fixture, and undocumented totals-exclude-root, CloudOnly-on-files-only and ScanResult.Root. The engine's stored design record still holds the pre-amendment text. The corrected text lives only in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md.

.taad/fitness.yaml was never written, so the Fitness gate saw NONE for the whole slice and validate recorded `Fitness op=check` as not-run. The five architecture rules are enforced only by ArchitectureRulesTests. The person deferred it; the gap is that nothing converts a design's declared architecture_rules into fitness.yaml.
Two numbers were noticed and never explained. The critique called C:'s 3 probe failures 'unexplained', and validate #3 shows 7. C:\ link count was 16,799 in attempt 1 and 16,486 in validate #3.

missed.what: Critique #1 was recorded as a pass without review ('low-risk slice, builder reviews its own work') on a scanner slice. The project constraint says scanner slices are cut above the default tier, and Q-002 had already raised SL-020 to medium. The skip check read the stale tier. Design errors that a real pre-build critique would have caught then reached the build: the inert 1314 P/Invoke fallback (m9), the non-existent ServerGarbageCollector MSBuild property, the unworkable deny-ReadAttributes fixture, a cloud-fixture test that passes without its rule (m3), and unpinned invariants M1 and M2.
missed.caught_by: critique #2, after build #1 had already shipped the design as code

missed.what: The design dropped the architecture's used-space comparison without recording it as deferred. The 14 findings, filed with the build's C: numbers in hand, did not mention that a drive-root scan's 'Finished' ended about 49 GB below the volume's used space. Part of that gap is $MFT and other metafiles no unprivileged listing can reach.
missed.caught_by: critique-review, which added M-add-1; fixed as O-013 with a coverage line in the window

missed.what: The Scanner.Scan contract used a bare ArgumentException for the relative-or-empty-root rejection. It did not ask which other code in the same call chain throws ArgumentException subclasses: ScanStore.At throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, and Path.GetFullPath throws with ParamName 'path'. Critique m6's fix ('any exception leads to Could-not-read') led to a window catch that showed an internal store indexing bug as 'Could not read'.

M3's prescribed fix (also probe files listed at 64 MiB or more) added a second cloud-guarded probe branch. The same critique's m3 had just flagged tests that pass whether or not the guard exists, yet the fix did not require a mutation-proof test for the new branch. Deleting `!cloudOnly &&` from SizeProbe.IsDue left all 86 tests green.
missed.caught_by: code-review #1 (m1), by mutating the code; fixed as O-014 in build #3

learned.lesson: When a person re-tiers a slice at a design halt (Q-002 low to medium), check that the critique and critique-review skip decisions are re-evaluated against the new tier before build starts. Otherwise the critique runs after the build and its findings become a rework lap.
learned.evidence: Header says 'medium · high risk', but critique #1 and critique-review #1 recorded 'a low-risk slice in a minimal project'. Critique #2 opened after build #1. Its 14 findings produced build #2 with 12 obligations (O-002 to O-013).

learned.lesson: A critique that runs after the build should be aimed at the diff and the tests, and must cite file:line for any claim about built behaviour. Its design-text findings partly restate fixes already in the tree, and its severities need a second look.
learned.evidence: m2 and m3 were accepted-fixed because the code already did it (DirectoryReader.cs:106-107, OnDiskSizeTests.cs:52-73). M2's claim about SizeProbe's path source was wrong (Scanner.cs:159). M1 and M2 were re-graded minor. M3's flushed-writer case was refuted by the documentary test in O-004.

learned.lesson: A minor obligation that is accepted-pending after code-review costs a whole build, review and validate lap. Discharge it before validate starts. Validate's real-drive battery (C:\ scan, D:\ and C:\Windows cross-checks, publish) is too expensive to spend discovering that obligations are still open.
learned.evidence: Code-review #2 passed with O-014 and O-015 pending. Validate #1 ran the full battery and halted on 'not in the tree'. Validate #2 failed on the same fact. Only validate #3 passed.

learned.lesson: In this codebase a scanner test can pass without the rule it names. The only reliable proof is a mutation: delete the guard, watch the named test fail, restore the file byte for byte. Any new branch in SizeProbe.IsDue, EntryClassifier or the size-probe path should ship with a recorded mutation check.
learned.evidence: m3 (offline fixture that never reached the guard) and O-014 (deleting `!cloudOnly &&` left 86 tests green) were found only by mutating. Validate #3 re-ran the mutation: Expected 2, Actual 3 probes.

learned.lesson: The tree slice must sum the store through ScanStore.ChargedSize(i)/ChargedOnDisk(i), never raw Size/OnDisk. Duplicates and Links charge 0, totals cover entries 1..Count-1 (the root excluded), a duplicate name still shows its own stale listing size, and a display accessor that follows a duplicate to its charged record is deliberately left to the tree slice. Rollups written on raw Size double-count hardlinks (WinSxS/System32) and nothing fails.
learned.evidence: O-002 and O-012, and the person's decision on M1 ('display accessor ... left to the tree slice, which is the first reader to show per-entry sizes').

learned.lesson: The next designer must read docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md, not the engine's stored design record. The stored record holds the pre-amendment text (HashSet<int> index, ServerGarbageCollector, the ReadAttributes-deny ACE fixture).
learned.evidence: Code-review #3 lists 'the engine's stored design record keeps the pre-amendment text, and docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md supersedes it in the repo' as declared standing drift. Critique m11 and O-012.

learned.lesson: The listing's size fields are unreliable in three measured ways. WOF files list AllocationSize 0 (142.6 MiB real), and the WOF filter hides the reparse bit and tag. The non-written hardlink name lists a stale EndOfFile. Actively written small files list stale sizes even after the 64 MiB probe rule (CldFlt1.etl was 12,288 B short on EOF and 118,784 B on allocation). Cloud placeholders are visible only via RECALL/OFFLINE attributes, and only 0xA0000003, 0xA000000C and the DFS tag 0x8000000A are Links. Any new reader of sizes must go through the scanner's probe rules and must not re-derive links from FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT (architecture rule, src/** minus EntryClassifier.cs and Native/Kernel32.cs).
learned.evidence: Spikes reparse-points-that-are-not-links and directory-listing-carries-on-disk-size-and-identity (both no-go); O-005, O-006 and O-004; validate #3's not-reached list.

learned.lesson: The engine guard now refuses UI Automation, and the App has no test project and no machine-readable outcome. A slice that adds UI (the tree) must design an observation seam up front, for example the outcome written to a file or stdout behind a flag, or an App test project. Otherwise validate can again only read a harness-hosted MainWindow, and the shipped exe's window stays 'not reached'.
learned.evidence: Build #3 not-run: 'PreToolUse guard refused... UI Automation'. Validate #3 used a throwaway WPF harness that raises Click in-process and reads TextBlocks. It observed the published exe only at process level (runs without a .NET 10 runtime, peaks 192 MiB).

learned.lesson: Every build, test and publish in this repo goes through `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 ...`. The machine has no .NET 10 SDK or runtime, so each fresh slice worktree downloads about 300 MB of SDK 10.0.401 into its own gitignored .dotnet/, and the first build step should show `eng/dotnet.ps1 --version` printing 10.x. Symlink and junction tests run unelevated under Developer Mode. The tests' %TEMP%\fsa-tests should be empty afterwards, and validate checks that.
learned.evidence: Build #1 and validate #1 'worktree had no SDK, so eng/dotnet.ps1 bootstrapped 10.0.401'; m10; Q-001 and Q-003; validate #3 confirmed %TEMP%\fsa-tests was left empty.

learned.lesson: A first slice from an empty tree that carries a project constraint forcing five counting-rule tests, plus a store contract that is expensive to reverse, should be sized large or cut into scaffold, scanner core and window. The follow-on slices (tree, rollups) start from a built store and are smaller. Do not size them by this slice's lap count.
learned.evidence: Medium sizing versus 3 runs each of critique, critique-review, build, code-review and validate, 2 each of design and spike, 15 obligations, and an 86-test suite.

unknowns: Does an unflushed, still-growing writer (WSL/Docker .vhdx, VM disk) show a stale listing size that the 64 MiB probe rule misses? The documentary test only covered Flush(true), and validate saw stale sizes on small actively written files (CldFlt1.etl).
What are the 7 probe failures on C:\ (3 in the critique's earlier run)? Are they denied or sharing-violation opens the probe cannot help, or a path-shape defect? Nobody has looked at one.
Why did C:\ show 16,799 links in attempt 1 but 16,486 in validate #3? Is that ordinary churn, or a classification difference? Core is unchanged since 2e4eb27, and the difference was not reconciled.

Does the FAT/exFAT listing fallback, including the empty-root case where ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND on the first call must mean an empty listing, work on a real volume? It was reached only on SMB, and the machine has no FAT or exFAT drive.
Should the tree slice keep the App in code-behind or move to a view-model? The design explicitly left this open for the next slice, and it changes what validate can observe.

candidates.title: Make a design's declared architecture_rules reach Fitness (.taad/fitness.yaml)
candidates.why: Deferred by the person (m3). Fitness reported NONE all slice, and validate recorded `Fitness op=check` as not-run. The five FsAnalyser rules (including the widened reparse rule and the interop-only-in-Native rule) exist only in ArchitectureRulesTests and docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. The gap is that nothing turns declared rules into fitness.yaml, so every later slice's gate will read 'no rules declared'.

candidates.title: Give validate a way to read the App's window state without UI Automation
candidates.why: The guard refused UIA mid-slice, so O-015's window behaviour was verified only indirectly and the published exe's own window was never read. Add a flag that writes the ending and totals to a file or stdout, or add an App test project. The tree slice adds screens and will need it.

candidates.title: Explain the unseen bytes on a drive-root scan (coverage breakdown)
candidates.why: M-add-1's decision left 'explaining the gap' to a later slice but named none. On C:\ the scan showed 53.3 GB of 746.3 GB in use as unseen and 599 unreadable folders. Validate requested read-denied-folders to measure how much of the gap those folders hold, and no criterion depends on it yet.

candidates.title: Measure listing staleness for unflushed growing writers on the real C: (WSL/VM disks running)
candidates.why: M3 was kept as a major, but the documentary test covered only the Flush(true) case. Validate saw stale sizes again on small actively written files (CldFlt1.etl: EOF 12,288 B short, allocation 118,784 B short). A file whose listing is stale and small could escape the 64 MiB probe threshold. Count files where the listing and the probe disagree, with a VM or WSL running.

candidates.title: Share the .NET 10 SDK across slice worktrees instead of re-downloading about 300 MB per worktree
candidates.why: eng/dotnet.ps1 installs SDK 10.0.401 into each worktree's own .dotnet/, and every slice gets a fresh worktree (build #1 and validate #1 both bootstrapped it). The machine has no .NET 10 SDK or runtime. Any shared location under the user's profile has to be checked against the engine's machine-boundary guard first.

candidates.title: Harden Cancel against blocked network and cloud calls (CancelSynchronousIo plus ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED 995 as cancellation)
candidates.why: m7 was deferred: Cancel is checked once per folder, so an unreachable SMB share or a populating cloud folder blocks a single call until the provider times out. The decision said it belongs to the first later slice that hardens network and cloud volumes, and 'the engine must route it' because none is named. It cannot be tested unelevated here.

candidates.title: Person-attended real-volume checks: an empty FAT/exFAT stick, the OpenFolderDialog click, and Windows 10
candidates.why: Validate #3 could not reach these: the app's drive list held only C:, D: (NTFS) and Z: (SMB). The empty-root ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND handling (m2) is confirmed in code but never run on a real volume. Only a person with a USB stick or admin can do these, and everything ran on Windows 11 build 26200.
